items.text: For buyers · Where the return now sits
Six and a half times in, nine times out. The end market decides whether that spread survives to exit.

The step-up between an add-on multiple and a platform multiple is what the market pays for scale in one end market, on the day you sell. The exit buyer will run the end-market work on your customer base.
What private equity paid for add-ons at $2M to $5M of EBITDA
Against 7.6 times at enterprise values of $25M to $50M, and 9.4 times at $50M to $200M.
Add-ons’ approximate share of US software private equity deal value
More than doubled. Platform buyouts fell to 41 percent of deal value, the lowest in at least a decade.
Software sponsor exits by value, first half of 2026
Roughly $32 billion on 111 deals. The number of deals was down 22 percent from the prior year.
Broken letters of intent that died on a finding outside the earnings work
Up from 19.1 percent in 2023, while financing fell from 21.3 to 10.7 percent. What ends deals has moved from the balance sheet to the business.

TagniFi PowerComps, Q2 2026; the multiples are the provider’s own figures, published in a piece written by its managing director. PitchBook, June 25, 2026. ION Analytics / Mergermarket, July 15, 2026. A lower-middle-market deal platform’s published study of broken letters of intent, January 27, 2026: seventy-five broken letters across eight buyer types and eight industries, with 2023 comparisons from the same series. The percentages are separate reported categories and are not summed here. That study covers all industries and does not break its diligence category down further.

items.text: Platforms and add-ons · What the desk does for you
Six things the desk does before a name reaches you.
The clock is running and the exit door is narrower. The desk makes each add-on a deal the exit buyer will not reopen.
The sector
Mapped for add-ons
Every company in the vertical your platform serves, with its owner, its size and its signals, before any of them goes to market.
The exit buyer’s read
Run early
The exit buyer will run the end-market work on your customer base. The desk runs it first, on each add-on, so the platform’s story holds at exit.
The owners
Known ahead of a process
Relationships built before a banker is hired, so the platform is already the natural home when the owner decides.
The evidence
Traced to source
Revenue reconciled to bank deposits, every adjustment marked supported or unsupported, before the letter is priced.
The integration risk
Read in the records
Contracts with consents, customers shared with the platform, systems that will not merge, found before the letter rather than after closing.
The fit
Scored against your thesis
Each business scored and ranked against criteria and weights you approved. You decide which to pursue.

sections.name: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.

items.text: Platforms and add-ons · Questions
Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.
Why does the return sit in the add-ons?

Because the platform multiple was paid at entry. The add-ons are bought at the sector’s multiple and sold at the platform’s, and the exit buyer prices the whole on the end-market work it runs on your customer base.
What does criteria on file ask of me?
Your criteria, confirmed with you each quarter. A dedicated search in one sector is by exception, with scope agreed in writing.
Can the desk cover more than one platform in a sector?
Yes. Criteria on file can cover more than one platform in a sector, and a dedicated search is scoped in writing for each engagement.
Do you represent the seller as well?
Never on the same transaction. Capital Row acts for one side, under a scope agreed in writing.
What is the first conversation?
Your thesis and the sectors that match it. One business day, read by a person.
